item.title: Berkwits '29: Collective effervescence is present on Brown's campus. Let's foster it.
item.description: The term "collective effervescence" was coined by sociologist Émile Durkheim in his 1912 book Elementary Forms of Religious Life. It is the unity formed when people are engaged in a shared purpose. It is the sensation when individuality comes second to collectivity. item.title: Rhode Island is giving up on climate
item.description: It's been almost five years since Rhode Island passed the ambitious Act on Climate, a seminal piece of legislation setting mandatory incremental goals to bring the state's carbon emissions to net zero by 2050. But today, the prospect of reaching those goals looks bleak. The state's public transit system is in shambles, the governor is cutting renewable energy funding and the electrification of vehicles and buildings lags behind our targets. If climate policy is war, Rhode Island is surrendering.
